description: Publish a web page: encode one self-contained HTML document (or fragment, or plain text) into an anew.page URL and return that URL. Use it when the user asks for a page, a site or a link they can open and share. The page is carried in the URL itself — no account, and no copy of the page is kept — so anyone who has the URL can open it; each call also starts a screenshot of the page, cached publicly for link previews. Put markup and inline CSS in html and any JavaScript in javascript as plain source; the server inserts it before </body>. Inline the page's CSS, scripts and images so it renders on its own; a webfont may load from a CDN. Each encoding path is deterministic: the same input through the same path always produces the same URL. Different paths use different Brotli encoders, though, so the same HTML may mint different — equally valid — URLs; compare pages by their decoded HTML, never by slug. Limits: a page past 65000 URL bytes or 1048576 decoded bytes is refused with an error, and a URL over 4000 bytes works but may be cut short by apps it is shared through — the result then carries a warning. To revise an existing anew page, its URL is its source: read it, edit that HTML, write it again. The new URL is a separate page and the original keeps working. Read it with anew_read first, then call this with the edited HTML.

html.description: The page: HTML markup with inline CSS — a full document, a fragment, or plain text. Its JavaScript goes in javascript. Encoded into the returned URL.

javascript.description: Optional client-side JavaScript for the page, as plain source without script tags. The server inserts it immediately before </body> (or at the end when there is no body).

name: anew_write

decoded_bytes.description: The submitted HTML in UTF-8 bytes.

url.description: The anew.page URL of the page.

warning.description: Present when the URL is over 4000 bytes: the page works, and some apps cut a link that long short when it is shared.

title: Write a page (HTML → anew.page URL)
